mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.2%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.2% (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL increase exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals rising inflation, prompting monetary tightening expectations that cause negative S&P 500 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances (CPIAUCSL rise > 0.2pp).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in employment (PAYEMS) and decreases in unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 60-day returns.
failure_condition: The joint condition (PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease) occurs but SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate).

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL index > 200), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns due to expectations of aggressive monetary tightening and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 200 (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate).

mechanism_narrative: High housing starts (HOUST > 550) indicate strong consumer demand and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when HOUST > 550 (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 95.0) signals weakening manufacturing activity, causing negative S&P 500 60-day returns due to reduced corporate profitability expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 95.0 (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in residential sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate robust consumer demand and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 20-day returns through elevated corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: The joint condition (RSAFS and HOUST increases) occurs but SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate).

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%), the S&P 500 produces negative returns due to reduced consumer spending, lower corporate earnings, and increased risk aversion.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0% (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate).
